newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude off with weak domestic market.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude off with weak domestic market.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices eased Thursday as domestic crude markets continued to weaken and local trade stagnated, traders said.
ARCO remained the only confirmed seller of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude for August, with three cargoes sold in July to Northwest U.S. refiners on a formula basis.
Formula deals, which are based on monthly price averages gathered by news services, do not affect the spot market price.

BP, the grade's main seller, offered at $1.85 a barrel under August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing crude. Buyers were seen bidding at much bigger discounts, around $2.16 under, in line with the last deal done in mid-June.
With the discount flat, outright prices for ANS crude oil fell with a weaker cash prices.
Line 63 barrels also eased in line with the NYMEX and cash crude.
Kern River and Wilmington crudes -- California heavy grades -- were unchanged.
Foreign spot buying remained quiet, traders said.
